records.issue_text: [BUG] The 'Plugin Request Completed' egress log line silently loses the traceID field because the old explicit `tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false)` lookup was deleted and nothing in the new FromContext path guarantees it is re-added. Operators and dashboards/alerts keyed on the grafana-data-egress log lines (e.g. joining a plugin egress event to a trace via traceID) get log entries with no traceID; the correlation requirement the previous code satisfied is dropped. It only survives if infra's ConcreteLogger.FromContext happens to re-derive it, which the diff never verifies.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] TestLogger.FromContext returns a brand-new NewTestLogger(), discarding both the receiver's state and all contextual attributes, so tests exercising FromContext can capture neither the logs emitted downstream nor the context enrichment. Anyone writing tests for the new LoggerMiddleware.FromContext path gets a fake that silently swallows assertions — Message/Calls stay zero on the new logger — producing tests that pass while verifying nothing.
records.rationale: The diff adds `FromContext` to the `Logger` interface and implements it on the fake: `func (f *TestLogger) FromContext(_ context.Context) Logger { return NewTestLogger() }`. This returns a brand-new logger instance, discarding the receiver `f` (its `Calls/Message/Ctx` fields) and any prior contextual state. Given `LoggerMiddleware` now logs via `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`, using `TestLogger` in tests would record logs on the new instance, leaving the original fake’s counters/fields unchanged—matching the finding’s “swallows assertions” mechanism.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The refactor silently drops the traceID, pluginId, and endpoint fields from the 'Plugin Request Completed' log line, replacing them only with attributes provided via the contextual logger — with no guarantee the fallback path carries them. Operators grepping 'grafana-data-egress' logs lose trace correlation (traceID) and endpoint identification for every plugin request whenever the contextual-attribute path is not populated; the grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext fallback at logger.go:51 returns d.New(), which carries none of these fields, so log consumers and any dashboards alerting on these fields break.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The rewrite of logRequest drops the traceID field from the "Plugin Request Completed" (grafana-data-egress) log line, and nothing in the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware re-adds it. The egress log previously correlated each plugin request to its trace via tracing.TraceIDFromContext; after this change operators querying the data-egress log by traceID get no matches, silently breaking log-trace correlation that existed before the rename. The contextual attributes added by instrumentContext (endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, uname) replace the removed fields, but traceID has no replacement source anywhere in this diff.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The refactor drops traceID from the 'grafana-data-egress' audit log with no replacement source. The old logRequest appended tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx) to every Plugin Request Completed event; the new version only relies on contextual attributes set by ContextualLoggerMiddleware, which adds endpoint/pluginId/dsName/uid/uname but no traceID (see contextual_logger_middleware.go instrumentContext). The 'grafana-data-egress' event consumers (audit/compliance pipelines that correlate egress log lines with request traces) lose traceID on every plugin request, and nothing in the diff surfaces that regression — the log line still emits 'status OK', so it reads as success.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext silently discards all contextual attributes when the infra logger is not a *log.ConcreteLogger. If d.l.FromContext(ctx) returns any non-ConcreteLogger implementation (infra log wrappers/mock loggers used in tests or alternate builds), the type assertion fails and the method returns d.New(), a logger with zero request context — every plugin-request log line then omits pluginId/endpoint/uname with no error, warning, or observable signal. The operation still logs 'successfully', so operators never learn their egress logs are unattributed. Rebuttal: 'ConcreteLogger is the only real implementation' — but the wrapper pattern here exists precisely because that is not guaranteed, and the fallback is silent rather than logged.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] TestLogger.FromContext returns a brand-new TestLogger instead of f, so all logs emitted via FromContext are invisible to the test's assertions. Any test that stubs a TestLogger into LoggerMiddleware and asserts on ErrorLogs/Calls for the new FromContext-based logging path sees zero calls — assertions pass vacuously and a future regression in the FromContext wiring would not fail any test. The strongest counter is 'callers can capture the returned logger'; that fails for middleware that calls FromContext internally and discards the original logger.
